blocks.text: Like function parameters, `match` works with modes. By default (`match s:`) it only reads the data. With `match lend s:` you can **change the data inside the variant in place**; the name in the pattern becomes a `lend` reference.
The third mode, `match consume s:`, takes ownership and moves the data to its new owners; it is used with variants containing types like `String`/`List`.

blocks.prompt: Write `double_it(c: lend Cell)`: if it is `Cell.Number(n)` it doubles `n`, if it is `Cell.Blank` it does nothing. Try it with `Number(21)` and print the result.
blocks.hint: Write `match lend c:` and `n *= 2` in the `Cell.Number(n)` branch.

blocks.q: Which `match` form changes data inside a variant in place?
blocks.why: `lend` is for changing; the default `match` only reads.
